annotations.text:
LiteTV config page — the whole thing, nine screens over two pages.

Built on your live theme: ElegantFin's own colours (#111827 ground, #775bf4 accent, Inter), with surfaces as white-alpha the way Jellyfin Enhanced does it — so it stays right if the theme changes. The tab pills with icons and the left-rule help text are lifted from Jellyfin Enhanced.

Most of it is clickable: the channel rail, the tab pills, Week/Day, the day picker, the (?) buttons, the order switch on Content, the shape filters on Look, the stage toggle on Breaks, the checkboxes and the mode switch on Suggestions.

Second page: making a channel, and the server.
The week answers "what shape is my week". Bars select; the inspector appears under the grid.
The day answers "what exactly happens at 20:15". 18:00–midnight, so a 30-second advert is a row you can grab.
Sources in play order, then the blocks — drawn as shapes on a week rather than three number fields. The right column shows how the settings would actually deal the queue.

No seconds box. Press "Show what happens while it works it out" to step through empty → asking → answered. The numbers are the real measured ones: the Avatar trailer is 2:28 long, has an 11.5 s outro, plays for 2:17.
Three pictures, each from an upload, the gallery, or a borrowed title — with a preview of how the television will actually draw the channel.
Every setting: plain label, one line, (?) for the real explanation. The right column warns these only shape a NEW week.

Two ways to start a channel, behind one switch — never both on screen, because they ask for different things.

Left: pick two or three things you like and it works out what they have in common. Right: tick libraries and genres. Both end in the same place — a proposed channel with a name, a count, and a typical evening you can read before you commit.
Everything that is not per-channel, in two: playback and trailers, and the builds this server hands the television. Both (?) marks open.
